objective: Stand up the Taylor Green vortex at Reynolds 1600 as the lab's externally graded unsteady dissipation instrument: two coarse rungs on the proven transient incompressible stack, no turbulence model, graded on the kinetic energy dissipation history against the published spectral reference at a tolerance declared before any solve
rationale: The repository has zero hits for the Taylor Green vortex; it is the cheapest canonical entry on the owner's new challenge slate and the only one that exercises the transient incompressible stack with no closure model in the loop, so the comparison is time integration and convection against a spectral reference and nothing else. That is exactly the instrument the pitching aerofoil family and the transient rotor branch will inherit: both report statistics of unsteady fields, and neither has a sibling anywhere in the lab where the transient integration itself has been graded against an external reference. Prediction, written before any solve: the coarse rung underpredicts the peak dissipation rate, because under resolution removes the small scales the peak lives on; the peak time lands within the declared tolerance at the fine rung; and the fine rung error is smaller than the coarse rung error on both quantities. One variable moves per rung, the mesh; the time step follows the declared Courant number, and a halved time step control at the coarse rung is priced in to separate temporal from spatial error before the mesh trend is read. Axis A: 3.0 gain points over 50 core minutes. Axis B: none at first filing; a clean trend is a candidate row against a published benchmark computation with no experimental anchor. Axis C: zero, no scored column moves
gate: Declared before any solve: the reference peak dissipation rate and its time from the published high order workshop reference data with provenance tier, the tolerance on each, and the two mesh sizes. PASS if the fine rung lands inside tolerance on peak time and the coarse to fine error shrinks on both peak value and peak time. FAIL, reported as a result, if the trend moves away from the reference. NO VERDICT if the halved time step control at the coarse rung moves the peak by more than the rung to rung increment, because the mesh trend is then not the thing being measured. If the workshop reference data cannot be fetched, the item stops BLOCKED at zero core minutes rather than grading against a digitised figure without saying so
cost_basis: estimate with no measured history in the family, stated as such: sized from cell count times step count against the lab's measured per cell per iteration rates on the same solver family, pricing a thirty three thousand cell rung, a quarter million cell rung and one halved time step control at the coarse rung, and explicitly not pricing a one hundred twenty eight cubed rung; overrun stops at the cap and the estimate is graded afterwards per the charter's factor three rule
expected_knowledge_gain: Three distinguishable outcomes, each changing a decision. A pass gives the lab its first externally graded transient integration and makes the case the standing regression anchor every future unsteady family inherits, which decides what the pitching aerofoil and transient rotor rungs are allowed to assume about the stack under them. A fail with a clean time step control is a real finding about the transient stack's dissipation at practical resolutions and caps what unsteady statistics the lab may claim until it is understood. A no verdict on the control means temporal error dominates at these resolutions, which reorders this family's ladder from mesh first to time step first before more compute is spent
citations: Brachet, M.E., Meiron, D.I., Orszag, S.A., Nickel, B.G., Morf, R.H. and Frisch, U., Small-scale structure of the Taylor-Green vortex, Journal of Fluid Mechanics 130, 411-452, 1983

van Rees, W.M., Leonard, A., Pullin, D.I. and Koumoutsakos, P., A comparison of vortex and pseudo-spectral methods for the simulation of periodic vortical flows at high Reynolds numbers, Journal of Computational Physics 230, 2794-2805, 2011

Wang, Z.J. and coauthors, High-order CFD methods: current status and perspective, International Journal for Numerical Methods in Fluids 72, 811-845, 2013, the first International Workshop on High-Order CFD Methods, whose Taylor-Green case at Reynolds 1600 carries the tabulated reference dissipation history
DeBonis, J.R., Solutions of the Taylor-Green vortex problem using high-resolution explicit finite difference methods, AIAA paper 2013-0382
The challenge slate of 2026-08, ranked program entry
launch_prompt: Taylor-Green vortex Re=1600, first rung. Solver: pimpleFoam (native openfoam2606), laminar (no turbulence model), nu=1/1600, cyclic cube of side 2*pi, standard TGV initial condition (u0=1, L=1 convention -- state the nondimensionalisation explicitly in the pre-registration, unit slips here are the classic failure). Step 1, zero compute: fetch the HiOCFD workshop reference data for the Re=1600 TGV (tabulated kinetic-energy and dissipation-rate histories; the 1st International Workshop on High-Order CFD Methods case files carry them, DeBonis AIAA 2013-0382 tabulates spectral values). If no tabulated reference can be fetched, stop and report BLOCKED at 0 core-min. Step 2: write the pre-registration -- reference peak dissipation rate and peak time, tolerances, mesh sizes (32^3 then 64^3), Courant number, and the dt-halving control at 32^3. Step 3: run 32^3 to t=20 time units writing volume-averaged KE every step (fieldAverage or a functionObject computing 0.5*mean(magSqr(U)); dissipation = -dKE/dt by central difference, state the differentiation stencil). Step 4: dt control at 32^3. Step 5: 64^3. Grade per the pre-registered gate. Budget 50 core-min, 8 ranks for the 64^3, setsid, retain logs + controlDict + the KE extraction script under demo-output/website/campaign/TGV_runs/. Evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/, docket update on this item.
